headline: Majors hold trend support as momentum softens; whales shift to cold storage after three weeks of accumulation onto exchanges.
paragraphs: The regime is intact but tired. All seven majors remain above their 200-day moving average, which is the structural floor for a bull market. Bitcoin is down 1.9% on the day but up 20.6% on the month and holds at 78,815, still 36.8% below its 12-month high of 124,740. Ethereum mirrors the pattern: down 1.6% today but up 26.6% over 30 days, holding above its 200-day line though 47.5% from its 12-month peak. The damage is deeper in altcoins: Solana is off 58.3% from its high, XRP down 55.7%, and Cardano down 76.6% year-to-date. The crosses tell a split story. Ethereum and Solana have golden crosses, suggesting their shorter-term trends have turned up relative to their longer-term ones. Bitcoin, XRP, and Dogecoin do not. This is not a picture of synchronized strength. It is a picture of a market still above its structural floor but showing fatigue at the day level.

Momentum against trend reveals the tension. RSI across the majors sits in the 57 to 66 range, elevated but not stretched. Bitcoin at 61.6, Ethereum at 61.8, and Solana at 62.0 are all in the upper half of neutral territory, meaning there is room to move without triggering overbought signals. The MACD picture is more revealing: Bitcoin, Ethereum, SOL, and XRP are all trading with MACD below signal, a bearish cross indicator that suggests upside momentum is receding. Binance and Dogecoin are the exceptions, both trading MACD above signal, which aligns with their stronger weekly moves (BNB up 6.5%, DOGE up 4.5% over seven days). This divergence is the finding: the largest, most liquid assets show momentum softening against a still-intact uptrend, while the smaller ones still have directional momentum in their favor. This is the texture of a rally that is broadening rather than accelerating.

Positioning in derivatives reveals crowded longs with expensive funding. Bitcoin perpetuals on OKX carry a long-to-short ratio of 1.14 and an 8-hour funding rate of 0.003% (annualized 3.2%), which is positive but moderate. Ethereum is tighter: 1.35 long-short ratio and 4.4% annualized funding, meaning longs are paying to hold. Solana shows the first crack: funding has flipped negative at minus 1.8% annualized, with the long-short ratio the highest in the cohort at 1.85, yet shorts are being paid to hold. This is a dangerous setup: extreme longs paying for the privilege of holding in assets that are richly valued relative to their range. The newest tension is on smaller names: XRP has a 2.48 long-short ratio with 6.7% funding, and Dogecoin has 3.38 long-shorts with 4.7% funding. These ratios are not small. Liquidations over the last hour or hours show longs being washed out across the board: Bitcoin saw 1.14M USD in long liquidations with zero shorts, Ethereum 2.04M in longs, and SOL 1.37M. This is how crowded positioning corrects.

Flow data shows a meaningful shift in whale behavior over the last 72 hours. Bitcoin moved 79.6M USD net off exchanges, ending a three-week cycle of buying onto spot. The weekly view makes this clearer: week ending August 17 saw 187M onto exchanges, August 24 saw 953M onto, August 31 saw 673M onto, and now the week ending September 7 shows 369M moving off. The biggest single move off was a 233M Bitcoin withdrawal from Coinbase repeated twice in the data. Stablecoin float sits at 310.6B USD, up just 1.45% over 30 days, which means dry powder has grown very modestly while whales have been rotating coins to cold storage. ETF flows into Bitcoin and Ethereum have been consistent: BTC took in 986.7M over the last five sessions (same-direction for three days), and ETH took in 215.3M (two days same-direction). This is traditional finance buying into spot while leverage and whale capital are repositioning. The tension is real: TradFi bid is steady and directional, but large holders are taking coins off-market and funding rates on levered long positions are inflating.

Sentiment reads as Greed at 71, within the upper half of its 30-day range of 27 to 74. This is the regime backdrop: the crowd is confident but not euphoric. The tape does not match this confidence. Every major except Binance and Dogecoin is trading with both MACD in bear cross and RSI still in neutral upper territory, a configuration that typically precedes consolidation or pullback. Bitcoin's 24-hour move is down 1.9% against a month that is up 20.6%, which means the crowd is optimistic about direction but the price is pausing or testing resistance. Altcoins are lagging their 12-month highs by 35 to 76%, which is a reminder that this is not a broad bull market yet, only a rally within a longer downtrend. The fact that whales shifted out of exchanges while funding rates remained elevated on major longs is the kind of disconnect that matters: the smart money is taking profits and moving to cold storage, while retail and levered accounts are still paying to hold positions.

Watch the MACD crosses on Bitcoin and Ethereum in the sessions ahead. If both move MACD above signal while RSI remains in the 55 to 75 band, the uptrend would have momentum confirmation. Watch also for a funding rate flip on Solana: if it moves from negative back to positive while the long-short ratio stays above 1.8, that would signal new longs entering a crowded trade. Monitor stablecoin float: if it accelerates meaningfully above 1.45% monthly growth while whale flows reverse back onto exchanges, that would be classic accumulation. The regime itself would break if any of the major four (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP) closes below its 200-day line on a daily close. Until then, the structure says trend is intact, momentum is softening, and the margin is where the real action is.
